title: Compose example trusts the whole shared bw-services subnet as reverse proxy and list reader
description: docker-compose.example.yml (the file README's quick start deploys) attaches the whitelister to BunkerWeb's bw-services network and sets TRUSTED_PROXIES to that entire /24 instead of the BunkerWeb ingress address; .env.example additionally allows /ips.txt from both subnets and leaves LIST_TOKEN unset. Any other container on bw-services, which in BunkerWeb's standard topology is every backend application the proxy publishes, is therefore treated as the ingress: it can connect to port 8080 directly (bypassing BunkerWeb's /login 6r/m limit and WAF), choose the client identity by setting X-Forwarded-For, which defeats the per-client login lock (only the process-wide 30 failures/minute budget remains) and forges the address in every audit line, and read the live whitelist from /ips.txt without any token. The application logic behaves as designed; the weakness is the deployment scope of the trusted-proxy and list-reader networks. Whether a lower-trust workload actually shares bw-services in the owner's stack is not visible in source.
claimed_root_cause: docker-compose.example.yml:16 and .env.example:14 define TRUSTED_PROXIES as the full bw-services subnet (10.20.30.0/24) that the whitelister joins at docker-compose.example.yml:22, rather than the single BunkerWeb ingress address or a dedicated proxy-only network, and .env.example:23-26 allow list downloads from the same shared subnets without the recommended LIST_TOKEN; config.py:192 turns that into a network allowlist that security.py:254-259 honours for any peer in it.

trace.description: The whitelister joins bw-services, BunkerWeb's network for proxied backends, which also carries bw-scheduler (line 57) and, in the documented BunkerWeb layout, every other published application.
TRUSTED_PROXIES=10.20.30.0/24 declares the entire shared subnet, not the ingress container, as trusted proxy (same value at .env.example:14).
LIST_ALLOWED_NETWORKS covers both compose subnets and LIST_TOKEN (lines 24-26) stays commented out, so any peer on either network downloads the list.
The subnet string becomes the trusted_proxies network tuple; list_allowed_networks and list_token are read at lines 212-213.

When the TCP peer is inside trusted_proxies the X-Forwarded-For header is honoured and walked from the right; a sibling container's self-chosen value becomes the client address. Verified in-sandbox: peer 10.20.30.77 with XFF 198.51.100.N resolves to that address (via_proxy=True), while peer 10.20.40.5 outside trusted_proxies has its XFF ignored.
throttle_key is derived from that forged address (app.py:318), so every request can present a fresh key; in-sandbox, rotating XFF yielded a distinct throttle_key per value.

The same subnet membership passes the /ips.txt peer gate: without forwarding headers and with no LIST_TOKEN the full active list is returned. Verified in-sandbox: the gate evaluated allowed=True for peers 10.20.30.77 and 10.20.40.5 with no headers, and False with a forwarding header or from a peer outside the list networks.

throttle.record_failure(key) (app.py:333) and audit_event (app.py:334) record the attacker-chosen identity; the per-client lock never engages across rotated values and only the global 30/min budget bounds guessing.

evidence.description: TRUSTED_PROXIES=10.20.30.0/24 with the comment 'the network BunkerWeb talks to us from' (whole subnet, not an address).
bw-scheduler, a non-ingress component, is attached to the same trusted bw-services network, showing the network is shared beyond the proxy.
LIST_TOKEN is commented out; the compose example does not set it either, so subnet membership alone grants /ips.txt.
Forwarding headers are ignored only when the peer is outside trusted_proxies; inside it the header is authoritative.
ips_txt allows any peer in list_allowed_networks that sends no forwarding header when list_token is None.
Quick start deploys docker-compose.example.yml directly, making it the maintained deployment path.

blockers: Not in source: whether any workload other than bunkerweb and bw-scheduler is attached to the bw-services network in the owner's deployment (BunkerWeb's documented stack attaches every proxied backend there; the example sketches only BunkerWeb components, and BunkerWeb's own source/topology is not present locally). This is the decisive lower-trust-entrypoint attachment and is only owner-observable.

Not in source: whether the BunkerWeb ingress container has a stable address (ipam ipv4_address) that TRUSTED_PROXIES could name instead of the /24, and whether BunkerWeb overwrites rather than appends X-Forwarded-For (remediation scoping).
Not in source: whether the live .env sets LIST_TOKEN (the example leaves it unset), which would close the list-disclosure part of the path.

validation_plan.local: Reproduced independently in the OS sandbox (TRUSTED_PROXIES=10.20.30.0/24, LIST_ALLOWED_NETWORKS=10.20.30.0/24,10.20.40.0/24, no LIST_TOKEN): resolve_client_ip('10.20.30.77', {X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.N}, trusted_proxies) returns (198.51.100.N, via_proxy=True) and throttle_key rotates per value, while resolve_client_ip('10.20.40.5', ...) ignores XFF (via_proxy=False); the /ips.txt gate (list_token None, no forwarding header, in_networks) evaluates allowed=True for peers 10.20.30.77 and 10.20.40.5, False with a forwarding header and False for 192.0.2.9. The hunter's full ASGITransport harness (agents/w1-h7-deploy-ci/artifacts/check-proxy-topology.txt) likewise shows 8 wrong-password POST /login from peer 10.20.30.77 with rotating X-Forwarded-For returning 401 x8 (no 429) with the forged addresses in the audit lines, and GET /ips.txt without headers returning 200 with the list. The source trace is confirmed and not refuted; only the deployment attachment is missing.
validation_plan.deployment: On the host, run `docker network inspect bw-services` and list the attached containers; if any container other than the BunkerWeb ingress (and scheduler) is attached, the trusted-proxy scope includes a lower-trust workload. Also confirm whether LIST_TOKEN is set in the live .env and whether the bunkerweb service has a fixed ipv4_address that could replace the /24 in TRUSTED_PROXIES. Observation only; do not send requests to the running service.

title: Entry policy tightening is not applied to stored rows: a password holder keeps, revives and makes permanent networks the current MIN_PREFIX_*/ALLOW_PRIVATE policy forbids
description: The container operator bounds what the shared-password operator may put on the BunkerWeb whitelist through MIN_PREFIX_V4/V6 and ALLOW_PRIVATE, enforced by parse_network. That check runs only in POST /entries. Rows accepted under an earlier, more permissive policy are still served verbatim by GET /ips.txt after the policy is tightened, and POST /entries/{id}/extend lets the logged-in operator extend them, revive an expired-but-retained one (counted from now) and set duration=forever so they never expire and are never purged, without re-running parse_network. Independently reproduced by the verifier in the sandbox: with ALLOW_PRIVATE=no and MIN_PREFIX_V4=16, POST /entries refuses 10.0.0.0/8 ('Networks must be /16 or smaller.') and 192.168.50.0/24 ('Private addresses are not allowed here.'), while POST /entries/2/extend duration=14 revives the expired 192.168.50.0/24 row and POST /entries/1/extend duration=forever makes the pre-existing 10.0.0.0/8 row permanent; /ips.txt then serves both and purge_expired never removes them. Principal: logged-in operator (password holder, lower trust than the container operator who sets the policy). Resource: the whitelist BunkerWeb enforces (networks on it skip BunkerWeb's security checks). Result: networks the current policy forbids stay on, return to, or become permanent on the list although the password holder could not add them today.
root_cause: whitelister/app.py extend_entry fetches the row with store.get (app.py:440) and writes the new expiry with store.set_expiry (app.py:461) without passing entry.network through parse_network(..., settings); duration=forever (app.py:445-446) removes the expiry outright and _extend_from (app.py:529-533) treats an expired row as extendable from now. ips_txt (app.py:302) and EntryStore.active_networks (entries.py:211-217) select by expiry only. EntryStore.__init__ (entries.py:107-126) and create_app (app.py:96-134) perform no re-validation of existing rows when settings change, so the policy is enforced exclusively at insertion time (the single parse_network call site, app.py:410).
intended_behavior: MIN_PREFIX_V4/V6 and ALLOW_PRIVATE (README.md:71-73, 133-134) describe the widest and the kind of networks allowed on the whitelist. README.md:32-33 states that expired entries stay visible, marked red and extendable until EXPIRED_RETENTION_DAYS, but does not say that extending bypasses the current entry policy. Any operation that makes or keeps a stored network active, in particular extend (including forever) and the list served to BunkerWeb, should re-apply the current policy; a row that fails it should not be extendable (and should be flagged or excluded from /ips.txt) until the container operator re-permits it or deletes it.

trace.description: Logged-in operator (session + same_origin + CSRF via require_post at line 437) submits duration and optional until for an existing entry id.
entry = store.get(entry_id): the stored network string is loaded but never passed to parse_network, so MIN_PREFIX_*/ALLOW_PRIVATE and the non-routable checks are not applied to it.
duration == 'forever' sets new_end = None with no MAX_DAYS cap and no policy check.
An expired row (expires_at <= now) counts from now, so an expired-but-retained row is revived by any day-based extension.
store.set_expiry(entry_id, new_end) persists the new (or NULL) expiry for the un-revalidated network.
UPDATE entries SET expires_at = ? WHERE id = ?: the row becomes active again or permanent (NULL expiry is never selected by purge_expired, entries.py:205-208).
render_list(store.active_networks(now)) serves every non-expired stored network string to the BunkerWeb scheduler; active_networks (entries.py:214) filters by expiry only.

evidence.description: parse_network is the sole implementation of the entry policy: min prefix (45-47), non-routable (48-49), private (50-51).
The only call site of parse_network in the package is add_entry (POST /entries); grep over whitelister/ finds no other (tests import it directly).
extend_entry loads the row and proceeds to duration handling (445-458) and set_expiry (461) without any network validation.
listed_entry is the only reader that re-parses a stored network, and only with ipaddress.ip_network for display matching, not with parse_network/settings.
EntryStore.__init__ only creates tables (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS); no migration or re-validation of existing rows on open.
min_prefix_v4, min_prefix_v6 (218) and allow_private (219) are read from the environment at each process start, so a tightening is an ordinary restart with changed variables.
active_networks selects by 'expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > ?' only, so a NULL-expiry row is served forever.
Syncer._run purges only rows with expires_at <= now - EXPIRED_RETENTION_DAYS via purge_expired (entries.py:202-209); active and NULL-expiry rows are never purged and the policy is not consulted.
Documented policy: networks wider than MIN_PREFIX_V4 / MIN_PREFIX_V6 are refused; README.md:133-134 call these the 'Widest allowed network' and ALLOW_PRIVATE 'Allow RFC 1918 / ULA entries'.

conditions.description: Attacker is a logged-in operator (holder of the single shared password) with a valid session and CSRF token; this principal is bounded by, but cannot change, the container operator's entry policy.

The container operator tightened MIN_PREFIX_V4/V6 or set ALLOW_PRIVATE=no (or otherwise tightened parse_network) after rows had been accepted under the earlier permissive settings, and did not manually delete those rows.

A row for the now-forbidden network exists in the SQLite entries table: active (extendable / forever) or expired within EXPIRED_RETENTION_DAYS (default 7) so it has not yet been purged and can be revived.

execution.attacker_perspective: A password holder notices that the operator tightened the entry rules (adding 10.0.0.0/8 or a private range is now refused) but that previously added rows are still listed on the page. Using the extend control on those rows they keep them active, bring an expired one back, or set them to forever, so the whitelist keeps networks the operator intended to no longer allow.
payloads: POST /entries  network=10.0.0.0/8  label=dummy  duration=30  _csrf=<token>   (phase A, ALLOW_PRIVATE=yes MIN_PREFIX_V4=8)
POST /entries  network=192.168.50.0/24  label=dummy  duration=1  _csrf=<token>   (phase A; then its expires_at moved 2 h into the past to make it expired-but-retained)
POST /entries  network=10.0.0.0/8  duration=7  _csrf=<token>   (phase B, ALLOW_PRIVATE=no MIN_PREFIX_V4=16: refused)
POST /entries/2/extend  duration=14  _csrf=<token>   (phase B: revives the expired private /24)
POST /entries/1/extend  duration=forever  _csrf=<token>   (phase B: makes the /8 permanent)
POST /entries/2/extend  duration=forever  _csrf=<token>   (phase B: makes the /24 permanent)
GET /ips.txt  from TCP peer 10.0.0.2 with no forwarding headers
instructions: Run the app in-process with httpx.ASGITransport(app, client=('10.0.0.2', 12345)) against a file-backed SQLite store in a scratch DATA_DIR, with WHITELISTER_PASSWORD, SESSION_SECRET, COOKIE_SECURE=no, TRUSTED_PROXIES=none, LIST_ALLOWED_NETWORKS=10.0.0.0/8, TZ=UTC and no BW_API_URL (API disabled, refresh_after_change is a no-op).

Phase A: load_settings + create_app with ALLOW_PRIVATE=yes MIN_PREFIX_V4=8; POST /login, read the _csrf token from GET /, POST /entries for 10.0.0.0/8 (30 days) and 192.168.50.0/24 (1 day); after the lifespan closes, reopen EntryStore on the same file and set the /24 row's expires_at to two hours ago via set_expiry (an expired-but-retained row).

Phase B: new load_settings + create_app on the same DATA_DIR with ALLOW_PRIVATE=no MIN_PREFIX_V4=16; GET /ips.txt; log in; POST /entries for 10.0.0.0/8, 192.168.50.0/24 and 192.168.50.1 and decode the wl_flash cookie of each 303 (itsdangerous URLSafeTimedSerializer, salt 'whitelister.flash').

POST /entries/<id of /24>/extend duration=14, POST /entries/<id of /8>/extend duration=forever, POST /entries/<id of /24>/extend duration=forever; decode the flash after each and read the rows' expires_at; control: POST /entries/999/extend; GET /ips.txt again; call store.purge_expired(now + 20 years).
Compare: the add path refuses both networks, the extend path accepts them, /ips.txt serves both, purge removes nothing.

remediation.strategy: Re-apply the current entry policy to the stored network on every path that keeps or makes a row active. Required: in extend_entry call parse_network(entry.network, settings) inside the existing try block so a row that fails the current policy is refused with the same alert flash as the add form (the operator must delete it or the container operator must re-permit it); this closes the demonstrated extend/revive/forever path. Recommended in addition, because an already-active forbidden row is still served until it expires: add EntryStore.policy_violations(settings), log a warning for each at startup in the lifespan, and either exclude those rows from active_networks (so /ips.txt matches the policy immediately) or surface them in the UI for deletion. Regression test: create 10.0.0.0/8 with MIN_PREFIX_V4=8 on a file-backed store, rebuild the app on the same DATA_DIR with MIN_PREFIX_V4=16, POST /entries/{id}/extend with duration=14 and duration=forever, and assert the 303 carries the prefix_too_wide alert and expires_at is unchanged (the two apps must not share one EntryStore object: the first lifespan closes it).

code_changes.fixed_code:
def test_extend_reapplies_current_policy(env):
    from whitelister.app import create_app

    # file-backed store in DATA_DIR (tmp_path) so a second app can reopen the same rows; no API
    env(ALLOW_PRIVATE="yes", MIN_PREFIX_V4="8", BW_API_URL=None)
    app = create_app(load_settings())

    async def go():
        async with app.router.lifespan_context(app), await _client(app) as c:
            await login(c)
            token = csrf_of((await c.get("/")).text)
            r = await c.post("/entries", data={"network": "10.0.0.0/8", "duration": "7", "_csrf": token})
            assert r.status_code == 303
            return app.state.store.find("10.0.0.0/8")

    entry = run(go())
    assert entry is not None

    env(ALLOW_PRIVATE="no", MIN_PREFIX_V4="16", BW_API_URL=None)
    app2 = create_app(load_settings())  # same whitelist.sqlite3, tightened policy

    async def go2():
        async with app2.router.lifespan_context(app2), await _client(app2) as c:
            await login(c)
            token = csrf_of((await c.get("/")).text)
            for data in ({"duration": "14"}, {"duration": "forever"}):
                r = await c.post(f"/entries/{entry.id}/extend", data={**data, "_csrf": token})
                assert r.status_code == 303
                assert "/16 or smaller" in (await c.get("/")).text  # alert flash rendered
                assert app2.state.store.get(entry.id).expires_at == entry.expires_at

    run(go2())

likelihood.reason: Requires a prior permissive period, a later tightening of MIN_PREFIX_*/ALLOW_PRIVATE by the container operator who did not also delete the affected rows, and a password holder who wants to keep them; the rows and every extend remain visible on the page and in the JSON audit log (entry.extend with network and expires_at), so the drift is detectable.

impact.reason: The password holder cannot add new forbidden networks; they can only keep, revive (within EXPIRED_RETENTION_DAYS) or make permanent networks that were previously allowed. Those networks (demonstrated: a /8 and a private /24) remain on the list BunkerWeb trusts and skips checks for, contrary to the current policy, until the container operator deletes them. No disclosure, no new principal, no escalation beyond the operator's existing whitelist authority.

confidence.reason: Complete source lineage (single parse_network call site at app.py:410, no startup re-validation, expiry-only selection in active_networks and purge_expired) and an independent in-process reproduction by the verifier on a file-backed store across a settings change, with the add path refusing and the extend path accepting the identical networks, and /ips.txt serving them.

title: A WHITELIST_URL that differs from WHITELIST_IP_URLS turns every revocation into a cache miss that the app reports as success; the example compose produces exactly that mismatch when the .env.example LIST_TOKEN recommendation is followed
description: The app invalidates BunkerWeb's derived copy of the list by DELETEing /cache/global/whitelist/whitelist-download/<sha1(WHITELIST_URL)>.list. On a 404 it POSTs /jobs/run and treats 200/202 there as full success: trigger_refresh sets last_success and clears last_error, api_state() renders 'ok' / 'API connected', and the delete handler flashes '<network> was removed.'. The client never reads the cache back (no GET /cache anywhere in bunkerweb.py although README.md:37 requires the cache_read permission), so a one-time first-run 404 and a 404 that persists because the computed name is not the name BunkerWeb keys on are indistinguishable to the app and to the operator. Verifier reproduction (sandbox, in-process ASGI app, httpx.MockTransport fake BunkerWeb answering per file name, check-1.txt): with LIST_TOKEN=abc, WHITELIST_URL=http://whitelister:8080/ips.txt and the fake holding only sha1('http://whitelister:8080/ips.txt?token=abc').list = 6251f2f0...e54d.list, the app DELETEd b563f953...d80f.list three times (startup, add, delete), got 404 three times, POSTed /jobs/run three times, flashed '203.0.113.42 was removed.', rendered header data-state="ok" 'API connected', client.status ok=True last_error=None, served /ips.txt?token=abc with 200 to the scheduler, and left the real cache file untouched. The control run with WHITELIST_URL equal to the scheduler URL (check-2.txt) produced byte-identical flashes and header state, so no in-app signal differs. The maintained deployment produces the mismatch through Compose precedence: docker-compose.example.yml:17 sets WHITELIST_URL in the whitelister service's environment: block, which overrides the env_file: .env value (line 13); .env.example:24-25 tells the operator to enable LIST_TOKEN and 'then set WHITELIST_URL to the same URL including the token', i.e. to edit the .env key that compose overrides. A real `docker compose config` render (Compose v5.6.1, inside the sandbox, no daemon; check-3.txt) of a project whose .env has LIST_TOKEN=abc and WHITELIST_URL=http://whitelister:8080/ips.txt?token=abc shows the whitelister service with LIST_TOKEN: abc and WHITELIST_URL: http://whitelister:8080/ips.txt. What the repository cannot establish is the impact on BunkerWeb itself: by the repository's own description (bunkerweb.py:3-5, README.md:26) the whitelist-download job skips the download while the cached file is younger than one hour, so if a job started through /jobs/run honours that skip, a deleted or expired network keeps bypassing BunkerWeb's checks for up to an hour while the operator is told the removal succeeded; if /jobs/run forces a fresh download, the mismatch costs only an extra job run and the finding reduces to a misleading status plus a dead cache_read requirement. Affected principal/resource: the holder of a revoked or expired network (lower-trust internet client) versus BunkerWeb's derived whitelist copy; the operator is the misled party.
claimed_root_cause: whitelister/bunkerweb.py:100-104 converts any 404 on the cache DELETE into a /jobs/run and reports a 200/202 there as success without ever verifying that a cache file under the computed name exists afterwards (no GET of the cache despite README.md:37 requiring cache_read), combined with docker-compose.example.yml:17 duplicating WHITELIST_URL in environment: so that the .env value the operator is told to edit (.env.example:24-26, 43-44) is silently overridden under the README quick start.

trace.description: WHITELIST_URL=http://whitelister:8080/ips.txt in environment: takes precedence over the env_file: .env value (line 13); confirmed by a real `docker compose config` render in the sandbox (check-3.txt). This is the maintained deployment's configuration source (README.md:90-91), not attacker input.

'(then set WHITELIST_URL to the same URL including the token)' instructs the operator to change exactly the key compose line 17 overrides; the scheduler's WHITELIST_IP_URLS (compose line 53, README.md:98) is changed to the token URL.
whitelist_url = _read('WHITELIST_URL') is taken verbatim (only the strip() in _read, line 43); nothing compares it with WHITELIST_IP_URLS, which the app cannot see.

name = cache_file_name(self.settings.whitelist_url) = sha1(token-less URL)+'.list' (b563f953...d80f.list), which differs from sha1(token URL)+'.list' (6251f2f0...e54d.list) that the scheduler created.
DELETE returned 404 -> POST /jobs/run (line 102); 200/202 returns normally (lines 103-104). Observed three times per run in check-1.txt.
Lines 90-92: last_success = now, last_error = None, pending = False: the persistent miss is recorded as a success.
With last_error None and last_success set, the header state becomes 'ok' / 'API connected' (index.html:2 renders data-state="ok").

refresh_after_change returned None (app.py:223-232), so the flash 'was removed' (locales/en.json:82) is shown although the cache file BunkerWeb keys on still exists; by bunkerweb.py:3-5 the re-run job skips the download while that file is younger than one hour.

evidence.description: cache_file_name = sha1(url.encode()).hexdigest()+'.list' over the exact configured string, no normalisation.
Repository's own statement (lines 3-5): the job keeps every URL under sha1(url)+'.list' and 'skips the download when that file is younger than one hour'.
A 200/202 from /jobs/run after a 404 returns normally and is indistinguishable from a successful cache deletion; the file contains no GET of /cache (only /ping, DELETE, POST /jobs/run).
whitelist_url = _read('WHITELIST_URL'); _read (line 43) only strip()s. The hunter's cite of line 430 was wrong: the file has 255 lines.
cache_read permission is required but never used: no GET of the cache file exists to verify the name.
'That job caches every URL for one hour.' The one-hour claim the impact depends on is the repository's own description of BunkerWeb, not verifiable locally.
env_file: .env; lines 14-18 then set TZ, TRUSTED_PROXIES, WHITELIST_URL and BW_API_URL in environment:, all four also present in .env.example (lines 53, 14, 44, 38).
WHITELIST_URL in .env, the value an operator edits per lines 24-25 and 43, is the one overridden by compose line 17.
Quick start runs docker compose -f docker-compose.example.yml with the copied .env (line 90), making this the maintained deployment.
The suite treats 404 -> POST /jobs/run as success; the FakeBunkerWeb (tests/conftest.py:33-36) answers 200 or 404 globally, never per file name, so a name mismatch is invisible to the tests.

blockers: BunkerWeb 1.6.17 behaviour is not in the repository: whether a whitelist-download job started through POST /jobs/run honours the one-hour cache skip described at bunkerweb.py:3-5 and README.md:26 (then the mismatch delays every revocation and expiry by up to an hour while the UI reports success) or forces a fresh download (then the mismatch only costs a job run and the finding reduces to a misleading status). This decides the impact and cannot be observed locally without BunkerWeb.

Whether BunkerWeb names the cache file sha1(URL exactly as written in WHITELIST_IP_URLS, including the ?token= query)+'.list'; the app assumes so (bunkerweb.py:3-4, 39) and the mismatch exists in this form only if that assumption holds. No BunkerWeb source is present locally.

Deployment drift requiring owner observation: the shipped files are consistent as-is; the mismatch arises only when the operator adopts the .env.example:24-25 LIST_TOKEN recommendation (and updates WHITELIST_IP_URLS) without also editing docker-compose.example.yml:17. Whether the real deployment runs with LIST_TOKEN set and compose line 17 unchanged is not visible in the repository.

title: One storage error in a Syncer tick permanently and silently stops expiry-driven BunkerWeb invalidation while /healthz stays ok and the UI shows only 'Refresh pending' or 'API connected'
description: Syncer._run (whitelister/bunkerweb.py:147-172) is the only code path that turns an entry's expiry into an invalidation request to BunkerWeb; explicit operator add/extend/delete call client.trigger_refresh() directly (app.py:223-232). The tick body calls store.expired_between() (line 160) and store.purge_expired() (line 164) with no exception guard; only client.trigger_refresh() (169-172) is guarded. A sqlite3 error raised by the shared connection on the /data volume (another process writing the database longer than the 5 s busy_timeout at entries.py:113, SQLITE_FULL, an I/O error) propagates out of the coroutine; the single asyncio task (started once at app.py:119-120, kept in self._task, no done-callback, no restart) finishes with the exception, which is never logged (the task stays referenced so asyncio never reports it; Syncer.stop() at bunkerweb.py:140-145 retrieves and swallows it at shutdown). From then on, for the life of the process: entries that reach their end are no longer reported to BunkerWeb, expired rows are never purged, and failed direct refreshes are never retried. GET /healthz (app.py:290-292) is a constant, so the Dockerfile:41-42 and docker-compose.example.yml:33-37 healthchecks keep passing; api_state() (app.py:234-242) reads only client.status, so the header shows 'Refresh pending' (when the failure hits purge_expired after expired_between already set pending=True, the realistic SQLITE_BUSY case under WAL) or 'API connected' (when the failure hits expired_between first, or after any later operator action whose direct refresh succeeds and clears pending). Verifier reproduction in the sandbox with a genuine 'database is locked' from a second connection holding BEGIN IMMEDIATE across the expiry tick (EXPIRED_RETENTION_DAYS=0 so that tick issues its purge DELETE): syncer task done with OperationalError('database is locked'), zero API calls after that entry's expiry and after a second entry's expiry (control run: DELETE /cache/global/whitelist/whitelist-download/<sha1>.list 2.5 s after expiry, entry purged), /healthz 200 {"status":"ok"}, header data-state="pending" 'Refresh pending', client.status.ok=True, last_error=None, no log record above INFO about the failure at runtime or shutdown (the only WARNING records are the two lifespan startup configuration notices for TRUSTED_PROXIES and COOKIE_SECURE), expired row still in the DB. The app's own /ips.txt already omits the expired entry (computed live, entries.py:211-217), so the loss is confined to telling BunkerWeb: the expired network keeps bypassing BunkerWeb's checks until BunkerWeb re-fetches the list on its own. Whether that happens after the documented one-hour download cache (README.md:33-34, bunkerweb.py:3-5) or never is BunkerWeb behaviour absent from the repository. No lower-trust principal of the app can cause the triggering fault: the store uses one in-process connection behind a threading.Lock (entries.py:108-113), all routes run on the event loop, and entries (5000 cap) and sessions are bounded, so the fault requires a container-operator-level or environmental condition on /data.
claimed_root_cause: whitelister/bunkerweb.py:160 and :164 perform the tick's store calls outside any try/except, and the Syncer has no supervision (single task created at bunkerweb.py:135 with no add_done_callback, no restart, no error flag on SyncStatus, exception swallowed at bunkerweb.py:144), so a single transient storage error becomes a permanent, unreported loss of the expiry-to-invalidation lifecycle contract that README.md:31-32 promises, masked by the constant /healthz (app.py:292) and an api_state() (app.py:234-242) that never reflects the task's liveness.

trace.description: The DELETE on the /data SQLite file is where an external storage condition enters the app as a sqlite3.OperationalError: another writer holding the database beyond busy_timeout=5000 (entries.py:113), SQLITE_FULL or an I/O error. Reproduced with a second connection holding BEGIN IMMEDIATE for 9 s: 'database is locked' after 5 s. The SELECT in expired_between (entries.py:196-199) is the read-side entry for I/O errors (under WAL a plain writer does not block it).

for entry in self.store.purge_expired(...): unguarded; the exception leaves the while loop and ends the coroutine before line 170 is reached. The DELETE is only issued when a row expired at or before now - EXPIRED_RETENTION_DAYS exists, so under WAL an external writer breaks the loop only during a purge tick (default retention 7 days).

for entry in self.store.expired_between(last_tick, now): likewise unguarded. In the observed run it succeeded first, logged 'entry expired' at INFO and set client.status.pending=True, which is why the header then reads 'Refresh pending' rather than 'API connected'.

The loop is one asyncio.Task kept in self._task with no add_done_callback and no supervisor; app.py:119-120 is the only call site (syncer.request_refresh(); await syncer.start()) and nothing restarts it. The reference in self._task also prevents asyncio's 'Task exception was never retrieved' report.

await self._task re-raises the stored exception only at shutdown and except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception): pass swallows it; observed: no record above INFO about the failure during runtime or at shutdown (only the two startup configuration WARNINGs emitted by the lifespan).

api_state() derives the header state solely from client.status (last_error, pending, last_success); the dead task leaves these untouched. Observed 'pending' / 'Refresh pending' after the writer-blocked failure; it becomes 'ok' / 'API connected' after the next operator add/extend/delete (direct trigger_refresh clears pending) or when the failure hits expired_between first (hunter's injected run).

GET /healthz returns the constant {"status":"ok"}; the Dockerfile:41-42 HEALTHCHECK and docker-compose.example.yml:33-37 healthcheck depend on it alone, so the container never turns unhealthy. Observed 200 {"status":"ok"} with the task dead.

await self.client.trigger_refresh() is never reached again: the App -> BunkerWeb API boundary receives no DELETE /cache/global/whitelist/whitelist-download/<sha1(WHITELIST_URL)>.list for the expired network (observed: zero API calls after the first and after a second entry's expiry, versus one DELETE 2.5 s after expiry in the control run), so BunkerWeb keeps serving the list it last downloaded until its own job re-fetches it.

evidence.description: Unguarded self.store.expired_between(last_tick, now) inside the loop body.
Unguarded self.store.purge_expired(now - timedelta(days=self.settings.expired_retention_days)) inside the loop body.
Only client.trigger_refresh() is wrapped in try/except Exception: pass.
self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._run(), name="whitelister-sync"): no done-callback, no restart, task kept referenced.
Syncer.stop swallows the task's exception at shutdown; nothing logs it earlier.
lifespan: syncer.request_refresh(); await syncer.start() is the only start; no restart path anywhere (no other reference to _task or add_done_callback in the package).
api_state() returns 'ok' from client.status alone; 'pending' while status.pending is set; never consults the task.
/healthz is the constant {"status":"ok"}; used by Dockerfile:41-42 and docker-compose.example.yml:33-37.

PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000 on the single shared connection: an external writer holding the database longer than 5 s makes the tick's purge DELETE (entries.py:208) raise 'database is locked' into Syncer._run.
The only write in a tick: DELETE FROM entries WHERE expires_at <= ?, executed only when purge candidates exist; the point at which the reproduced OperationalError entered the loop.
Product promise: 'A background loop watches for entries that reach their end, triggers the same refresh, and deletes expired entries after EXPIRED_RETENTION_DAYS'.

'Without the API the hourly job still picks the list up on its own': the project's own (not source-verifiable) statement that bounds the stale window to about one hour if BunkerWeb behaves as documented.

blockers: Decisive: BunkerWeb 1.6.17 behaviour is not in the repository. Whether the whitelist-download job re-fetches WHITELIST_IP_URLS on its own schedule once its one-hour cache (bunkerweb.py:3-5, README.md:33-34) is older than one hour, or only re-downloads when the cache file is deleted or the job is run through the API, decides whether an expired network keeps bypassing BunkerWeb's checks for up to about one hour (the same limit the README documents for API-off mode, making this a silent degradation to that mode for expiries only) or indefinitely until the next operator add/extend/delete or a container restart. The app side (no DELETE ever sent after the fault) is fully demonstrated locally; this external fact fixes the impact.

Likelihood only, owner-observed: how often a storage fault reaches the tick's store calls in the owner's deployment. Source shows no lower-trust trigger (one in-process connection behind a lock, bounded entries and sessions), so the trigger is an external writer on the mounted /data/whitelist.sqlite3 holding a write lock longer than 5 s during a tick that has rows to purge (under WAL a plain writer does not block the tick's SELECTs), a full /data volume at that DELETE, or an I/O error on either query. The same fault hitting an operator request would surface as a 500, but one confined to the background tick is invisible.

validation_plan.local: Re-runnable through the sandbox runner from the v3-4 scratch directory: python harness_v34.py with WHITELISTER_PASSWORD=correct-horse-battery-staple SESSION_SECRET=<40 x 'x'> DATA_DIR=. COOKIE_SECURE=no TRUSTED_PROXIES=none BW_API_URL=http://bw-api:8888 BW_API_USERNAME=admin BW_API_PASSWORD=secret WHITELIST_URL=http://whitelister:8080/ips.txt SYNC_DEBOUNCE_SECONDS=0 TZ=UTC EXPIRED_RETENTION_DAYS=0. It builds the app in-process (create_app with a file-backed WAL EntryStore in scratch and a fake BunkerWeb via httpx.MockTransport), runs the lifespan, sets Syncer.interval to 0.5 s, logs in, inserts an entry expiring in 2 s and, in the lock scenario, starts a thread whose own sqlite3 connection holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE for 9 s across that expiry; it then records API calls after expiry, task state/exception, /healthz, the header data-state, client.status, /ips.txt, purge state, log records, and whether a second entry's expiry still produces a DELETE. Expected: control run shows DELETE of b563f953e7c6fe56e62dd212cad4d10b4449d80f.list about 2.5 s after expiry and 'expired entry removed'; lock run shows task done with OperationalError('database is locked'), no API call after either expiry, /healthz 200 ok, header 'pending'/'Refresh pending', status.ok=True, no record above INFO other than the two startup configuration WARNINGs (TRUSTED_PROXIES empty, COOKIE_SECURE=no). Output as written to scratch check-1.txt (predeclared for promotion).
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed, non-destructive, on a staging BunkerWeb 1.6.17 stack built from docker-compose.example.yml with a throwaway whitelister database: (1) start the whitelister with EXPIRED_RETENTION_DAYS=0 (so the tick after an expiry performs its purge DELETE; with the default 7 days a fresh test entry never makes the tick write under WAL, and an external lock alone will not fail it) and add a test entry for an unused network with a 'date' duration ending at the next end-of-day in TZ (or a 1-day entry and wait). (2) About one minute before that end, from a host shell open sqlite3 on the mounted /data/whitelist.sqlite3, run BEGIN IMMEDIATE; and keep the shell open until at least 40 s after the entry's end (one 30 s tick plus the 5 s busy_timeout), then ROLLBACK; (3) Verify in docker logs: an INFO 'entry expired: <network>' line and no WARNING/ERROR afterwards; docker inspect still reports healthy; the UI header shows 'Refresh pending' (and 'API connected' after any later add/delete); the bw-api access/scheduler log shows no DELETE /cache/global/whitelist/whitelist-download/<sha1>.list and no POST /jobs/run at or after the entry's end. (4) Add a second short test entry and confirm its expiry also produces no API call, while an add/delete by the operator still does. (5) Decisive observation: from the expired test network, send requests through BunkerWeb and record for how long they are still whitelisted; in parallel watch the whitelist-download cache file (GET /cache/global/whitelist/whitelist-download/<sha1>.list with the API user's cache_read permission, or the scheduler log) to see whether BunkerWeb re-downloads /ips.txt on its own once the file is older than one hour. If it does, the stale window is bounded to about one hour; if not, it lasts until the next operator change or restart.

title: IPv6 scope id with an embedded newline passes parse_network and is written verbatim to /ips.txt, letting a logged-in operator list addresses the entry policy refuses
description:
parse_network validates the parsed ipaddress object (prefix length, multicast/unspecified/loopback/reserved, private when ALLOW_PRIVATE=no) but never inspects the text of an IPv6 scope id. Python's ipaddress (pinned venv, 3.13.17) accepts any scope id that is non-empty and contains no second '%', so '2a00::1%x
127.0.0.1' parses as the single host 2a00::1 with scope 'x
127.0.0.1'. network_text then returns str(net.network_address), which re-appends '%' + scope verbatim, and that multi-line string is stored in the UNIQUE network column, returned by active_networks and joined with '
' by render_list. GET /ips.txt therefore serves the refused address as its own line for BunkerWeb's whitelist-download job. Independently reproduced in the sandbox: a direct POST of 127.0.0.1 (default settings) and of 10.0.0.1 (ALLOW_PRIVATE=no) stores nothing, while '2a00::1%x
127.0.0.1' and '2a00::1%x
10.0.0.1' each return 303, store one row and make /ips.txt serve '127.0.0.1' / '10.0.0.1' as separate lines. At unit level the same mechanism carries comment lines ('2a00::1%x
# injected
224.0.0.1' -> three lines). Injected IPv4 CIDRs are not possible under the default MIN_PREFIX_V6=48 because any trailing '/n' is parsed as the IPv6 prefix of the whole string ('2a00::%x
10.0.0.0/8' is refused as prefix_too_wide). A plain scoped host such as 'fe80::1%eth0' is also stored and served with its '%eth0' suffix.
root_cause: whitelister/entries.py network_text() serialises a single-host IPv6 network with str(net.network_address) (and an aligned IPv6 network with str(net)), which includes the RFC 4007 scope id; ipaddress.ip_network in parse_network accepts a scope id containing newline, carriage return, NUL, '#' or any character other than '%'. Neither parse_network nor render_list rejects scope ids or checks that each emitted list line is a single address token, so the per-line policy enforced on the parsed object does not apply to the text actually written.
intended_behavior: Every line of /ips.txt after the header is exactly one address or CIDR that passed parse_network's prefix, routability and private-address policy (README.md security model: loopback, multicast, unspecified and reserved ranges are refused; ALLOW_PRIVATE=no refuses private ranges).

trace.description: Logged-in operator submits the urlencoded `network` form field; a %0A in the body decodes to a literal newline inside the value.
parse_network(network, settings) is the only validation applied to the value; line 411 then calls network_text(net).

ipaddress.ip_network(text, strict=False) accepts '2a00::1%x\n127.0.0.1' as host 2a00::1 with scope id 'x\n127.0.0.1'; lines 45-51 check prefix, routability and privacy on the parsed object only (2a00::1 is routable), never on the scope text.
For num_addresses == 1 returns str(net.network_address), which IPv6Address.__str__ renders as address + '%' + scope id verbatim, i.e. '2a00::1%x\n127.0.0.1'.
store.upsert(text, ...) writes the multi-line string into the UNIQUE `network` column via a parameterised INSERT.
SELECT network ... returns the stored column verbatim for every unexpired entry.
After the peer / forwarding-header / token gate, render_list(store.active_networks(now)) is served as text/plain to the BunkerWeb scheduler.
'\n'.join(['# bunkerweb-whitelister', *networks]) emits the raw stored strings; the embedded newline turns the scope text into additional list lines with no re-validation.

evidence.description: Sandbox probe on the pinned interpreter (3.13.17): ipaddress.ip_network('2a00::1%x\n127.0.0.1', strict=False) succeeds, prefixlen 128, network_address.scope_id == 'x\n127.0.0.1', is_loopback False; '2a00::1%x%y' and '2a00::1%' raise ValueError (only a second '%' or an empty scope is refused).

The routability/private checks run on the parsed object: parse_network('127.0.0.1') raises error.ip_not_routable while parse_network('2a00::1%x\n127.0.0.1') returns a network and network_text() of it is the two-line string '2a00::1%x\n127.0.0.1'.

network_text keeps the scope id: observed stored values '2a00::1%x
127.0.0.1', '2a00::1%x
# injected
224.0.0.1' (3 lines) and 'fe80::1%eth0'; '2a00::%x
10.0.0.0/8' is refused with error.prefix_too_wide because '/8' becomes the IPv6 prefix.

render_list performs no per-line validation; sandbox GET /ips.txt returned 200 with body '# bunkerweb-whitelister
2a00::1%x
127.0.0.1
' after the injected POST (check-1-repro.txt).

Security model states loopback, multicast, unspecified and reserved ranges are refused; the sandbox run shows 127.0.0.1 served as a list line under default settings and 10.0.0.1 served under ALLOW_PRIVATE=no although both are refused when posted directly.

conditions.description: Requires a logged-in operator session (knowledge of the shared password) plus the session's CSRF token and a same-origin request; what is bypassed is the configured entry policy, not authentication or CSRF.

Under the default MIN_PREFIX_V6=48 only single hosts, comment/arbitrary text lines and IPv6 CIDRs with prefix >= 48 can be injected, because a trailing '/n' is applied to the carrier IPv6 address; injecting IPv4 CIDRs such as 10.0.0.0/8 would additionally require MIN_PREFIX_V6 <= 8 (prefix >= MIN_PREFIX_V6).

Whether BunkerWeb actually honours an injected line depends on its whitelist-download job's own per-line parsing; no BunkerWeb source is in the repository and the downstream effect was not observed locally. The demonstrated result ends at the text served by /ips.txt.

execution.attacker_perspective: A person holding the whitelister password (any logged-in operator) wants to whitelist a host that the deployment's entry policy refuses, e.g. a loopback host or, under ALLOW_PRIVATE=no, a private host, or wants to append arbitrary lines to the list BunkerWeb downloads.
instructions: Run the app with default entry settings (TRUSTED_PROXIES=10.0.0.0/8, COOKIE_SECURE=no, SESSION_SECRET of >= 32 chars, WHITELISTER_PASSWORD of >= 12 chars, a fake BunkerWeb API or no BW_API_URL) and send requests from a peer inside LIST_ALLOWED_NETWORKS, e.g. 10.0.0.2.
POST /login with the password; GET / and read the hidden _csrf value from the form.
Control: POST /entries with network=127.0.0.1, duration=7 and the token; confirm no entry row exists and GET /ips.txt (no forwarding headers) returns only '# bunkerweb-whitelister'.
POST /entries with network='2a00::1%x' + newline + '127.0.0.1' (urlencoded 2a00::1%25x%0A127.0.0.1), duration=7 and the token.

GET /ips.txt from the allowed peer without forwarding headers and split the body on newline; repeat the control and injection with network=10.0.0.1 / '2a00::1%x\n10.0.0.1' in a deployment started with ALLOW_PRIVATE=no.
execution.observed_result:
Sandboxed in-process run (httpx.ASGITransport, in-memory EntryStore, MockTransport fake BunkerWeb API, Python 3.13.17, httpx 0.28.1, peer 10.0.0.2): control POST /entries network=127.0.0.1 -> 303, stored rows [], GET /ips.txt -> 200 '# bunkerweb-whitelister
'. Injection POST /entries network='2a00::1%x
127.0.0.1' -> 303, stored rows [{'id': 1, 'network': '2a00::1%x
127.0.0.1', 'label': 'probe'}], GET /ips.txt -> 200 with lines ['# bunkerweb-whitelister', '2a00::1%x', '127.0.0.1']. With ALLOW_PRIVATE=no: direct 10.0.0.1 -> stored rows [], list unchanged; '2a00::1%x
10.0.0.1' -> 303, one row, /ips.txt lines ['# bunkerweb-whitelister', '2a00::1%x', '10.0.0.1']. The audit line JSON-escapes the newline ('"network": "2a00::1%x\n127.0.0.1"'). Unit level: parse_network+network_text of '2a00::1%x
# injected
224.0.0.1' yields a three-line stored string; '2a00::%x
10.0.0.0/8' is refused (prefix_too_wide).

remediation.strategy: Refuse IPv6 scope ids at the parser and make the list writer defensive. In parse_network reject any input containing '%' or interior whitespace before calling ipaddress, and additionally reject a parsed IPv6 network whose network_address.scope_id is not None (scope ids are never meaningful for a reverse-proxy whitelist). In render_list emit only values that are printable, contain no whitespace or '%', and round-trip through ipaddress.ip_network, so rows stored before the fix cannot add lines. Add regression tests: parse_network('2a00::1%x\n127.0.0.1') and parse_network('fe80::1%eth0') raise error.ip_invalid, and every non-header line of render_list output parses as a single network. Verified in the sandbox against the current code: the re-implemented parser refuses all scope-id variants (LF, CRLF, NUL, aligned CIDR) while 1.2.3.4, 203.0.113.42/24, 2a00::1, 2001:db8::/48 and ::ffff:1.2.3.4 are still accepted unchanged, and the defensive render_list drops legacy multi-line rows.

likelihood.reason: Needs the operator password, a valid session and its CSRF token; that principal is already entitled to whitelist any routable network, so the only thing gained is bypass of the configured refusal of loopback/multicast/unspecified/reserved/private ranges and the ability to add free-text lines. The payload is trivial once logged in.

impact.reason: Demonstrated effect is limited to the text of /ips.txt: a policy-refused single host (or comment/arbitrary line, or an IPv6 CIDR >= MIN_PREFIX_V6) is served to the BunkerWeb scheduler. No wider-than-MIN_PREFIX IPv4 range can be injected under default configuration, the actor is an authenticated operator, the audit trail still records the full value, and BunkerWeb's acceptance of the injected line was not observed.

confidence.reason: Independently reproduced end-to-end in the OS sandbox with the pinned interpreter and dependencies: ipaddress scope-id behaviour, parse_network/network_text output, the stored row and the served /ips.txt body were all observed directly, and the trace is complete inside the repository. Only the BunkerWeb-side consequence is unverified and is recorded as a condition.
